subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an internal source of finance?
questions.explain: Retained profit is generated within the business, making it an internal source of finance.

questions.q: Why might a small business find it difficult to raise finance by selling shares?
options: Shares can only be sold by public limited companies to the general public
Retained profit must be used first by law
Sole traders always have unlimited capital
questions.explain: Only public limited companies can sell shares to the general public via the stock exchange, so small unincorporated businesses cannot access this source.

questions.q: What is meant by 'trade credit' as a source of finance?
options: A loan repayable over more than one year
Buying goods from suppliers and paying for them later
questions.explain: Trade credit allows a business to obtain goods now and pay the supplier at a later agreed date, a short-term source of finance.

questions.q: Which source of finance is most suitable for purchasing a long-term fixed asset such as machinery?
questions.explain: Long-term assets should be financed by long-term sources such as a bank loan so repayments match the asset's useful life.

questions.q: A business needs money quickly to cover a short-term cash shortage of one week. Which source is most appropriate?
questions.explain: An overdraft is a flexible short-term source ideal for covering temporary, short-lived cash shortages.

questions.q: What does a cash-flow forecast show?
options: The profit a business will make over a year
The expected flow of cash into and out of a business over a future period
The value of a business's assets and liabilities
The market share of a business
questions.explain: A cash-flow forecast predicts the timing and amount of cash inflows and outflows for a future period.

questions.q: In a cash-flow forecast, how is the closing balance calculated?
options: Opening balance plus net cash flow
Net cash flow minus total outflows
questions.explain: The closing balance equals the opening balance plus the net cash flow (inflows minus outflows) for the period.

questions.q: What is 'working capital'?
questions.explain: Working capital is the finance available for day-to-day running, calculated as current assets minus current liabilities.

questions.q: A cash-flow forecast shows a negative closing balance in March. What action could the business take to avoid this?
options: Increase the length of trade credit given to customers
Arrange a bank overdraft in advance
Buy more fixed assets for cash
questions.explain: Arranging an overdraft in advance provides cash to cover the forecast shortfall in March.

questions.q: Why is it important to distinguish between cash and profit?
options: Cash and profit are always identical figures
A profitable business can still run out of cash and fail
Profit is only earned when cash is received immediately
questions.explain: Because of credit transactions and timing, a profitable business may lack the cash to pay its bills and become insolvent.

questions.q: How is gross profit calculated in an income statement?
questions.explain: Gross profit is revenue (sales) minus the cost of sales (cost of goods sold).

questions.q: What is another common name for the income statement?
questions.explain: The income statement is traditionally known as the profit and loss account.

questions.q: How is profit for the year (net profit) derived from gross profit?
options: By adding cost of sales to gross profit
By subtracting expenses (overheads) from gross profit
By subtracting revenue from gross profit
By adding dividends to gross profit
questions.explain: Profit for the year is found by deducting a business's expenses or overheads from its gross profit.

questions.q: A business has revenue of $80,000 and cost of sales of $50,000. What is its gross profit?
questions.explain: Gross profit = revenue minus cost of sales = $80,000 - $50,000 = $30,000.

questions.q: What does a statement of financial position show?
options: The cash inflows and outflows over a year
The value of assets, liabilities and capital at a point in time
The revenue and expenses over a year
The forecast profit for the next year
questions.explain: The statement of financial position (balance sheet) records a business's assets, liabilities and capital at a specific date.

questions.q: Which of the following is a current asset?
questions.explain: Inventory is a current asset because it is expected to be turned into cash within one year.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as a non-current (fixed) liability?
questions.explain: A non-current liability is a debt repayable in more than one year, such as a five-year bank loan.

questions.q: How is the gross profit margin calculated?
questions.explain: The gross profit margin expresses gross profit as a percentage of revenue.

questions.q: What does the current ratio measure?
options: A business's profitability over a year
A business's ability to pay its short-term debts
The value of a business's fixed assets
questions.explain: The current ratio (current assets / current liabilities) measures liquidity, the ability to meet short-term liabilities.

questions.q: A business has current assets of $40,000 and current liabilities of $20,000. What is its current ratio?
questions.explain: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = $40,000 / $20,000 = 2:1.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies (0450) syllabus; Financial Information and Decisions
